title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten recurring Duquesne traditions documented by the university, from student-run Orientation and Cram Cooper to Ring Blessing and Festival on the Bluff.

cards.title: Spend Burgh Bucks at Orientation
cards.subtitle: Student leaders welcome new Dukes, then cap the week with an auction
cards.notes: Join Orientation activities to earn Burgh Bucks, then follow the published program for the week-ending Burgh Buck Auction.
cards.short_summary: Duquesne’s student-led welcome week turns participation into auction currency.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne says Orientation is designed and executed almost entirely by students; participants can earn Burgh Bucks through involvement and use them in a week-ending auction.
cards.access_notes: Intended for incoming students; consult the current Orientation program for event locations and participation details.

cards.title: Watch Fall Carnival Take the Stage
cards.subtitle: A former Greek variety-show showcase turned campus-wide autumn celebration
cards.notes: Look for the annual student performances and seasonal activities when Duquesne publishes the Fall Carnival program.
cards.short_summary: An older variety-show format lives on as Duquesne’s campus-wide fall gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne identifies Fall Carnival as an annual campus-wide tradition that began as a stage for variety shows by Greek organizations and now includes seasonal fun and performances.
cards.access_notes: The traditions page does not state a date, venue, admission policy, or attendance eligibility; check the current event listing.

cards.title: Help Cram Cooper
cards.subtitle: Students pack UPMC Cooper Fieldhouse to open basketball season
cards.notes: Wear Duquesne colors and join the student section when the current Cram Cooper game and entry details are announced.
cards.short_summary: The Dukes open basketball season with a student turnout tradition named for its venue.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne describes Cram Cooper as a tradition that starts basketball season by bringing students together to pack UPMC Cooper Fieldhouse in support of the Dukes.
cards.access_notes: Held at UPMC Cooper Fieldhouse; verify the current game date, ticket requirements, and student-entry rules before attending.

cards.title: See the Bluff Switch On for Christmas
cards.subtitle: Campus lighting, carols and carriage rides launch Duquesne’s holiday season
cards.notes: Arrive for the campus lighting, then follow the announced program for carols, carriage rides and the Union Ballroom feast.
cards.short_summary: Duquesne marks the holiday season by illuminating campus as one community.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne calls Night of Lights its annual holiday-season kickoff, featuring the campus lighting, Christmas carols, carriage rides, a photo booth and Santa’s workshop.
cards.access_notes: The entire University community is invited; the official page does not provide the current date, start time, or cost details.

cards.title: Trade Textbooks for the Christmas Ball
cards.subtitle: Duquesne students close the fall semester with a formal dance
cards.notes: Plan formal attire and confirm the current student registration, venue and guest rules before joining the December celebration.
cards.short_summary: A December formal gives Duquesne students a ceremonial close to fall classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne documents the Christmas Ball as a December tradition where students gather for a formal celebration near the close of the fall semester.
cards.access_notes: Described for Duquesne students; verify the current date, venue, registration requirements, guest policy and admission cost.

cards.title: Trace Duquesne’s Spiritan Foundations
cards.subtitle: A spring week of events honors the university’s founders and mission
cards.notes: Choose a published reflection, service or educational program to explore how Duquesne interprets its Spiritan foundations.
cards.short_summary: Duquesne revisits its founding principles through a recurring week of campus programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne says Founders Week is an annual tradition featuring events, reflections and celebrations focused on its Spiritan founders and values of service, faith, justice and education.
cards.access_notes: Programming varies across the week; consult the current schedule for individual venues, eligibility and registration requirements.

cards.title: Play All 10 Rounds of Epic Bingo
cards.subtitle: Hundreds of students gather for a prize-backed annual game
cards.notes: Watch student-life announcements for the venue and entry process, then bring your attention through all 10 bingo rounds.
cards.short_summary: Duquesne scales a familiar game into a ten-round student tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne identifies Epic Bingo as an annual event for hundreds of students consisting of 10 rounds of bingo with prizes.
cards.access_notes: Described as a student event; the official page does not provide the current venue, date, capacity, registration or cost.

cards.title: Close the Year at Festival on the Bluff
cards.subtitle: Live music, food and games fill campus at the end of spring
cards.notes: Check the end-of-year announcement for performers and activity locations, then plan an evening around the campus program.
cards.short_summary: Duquesne’s spring finale turns the Bluff into an end-of-year music festival.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne describes Festival on the Bluff as its end-of-year music festival, bringing students together on campus for live music, food, games and celebration.
cards.access_notes: Described as a student gathering on campus; verify the current date, event footprint, eligibility and admission details.

cards.title: Carry the Duquesne Ring into the World
cards.subtitle: Students gather to bless a symbol of their years on the Bluff
cards.notes: Order or bring the designated Duquesne ring and follow the ceremony announcement for eligibility and participation instructions.
cards.short_summary: A blessing links the Duquesne ring to the university’s values and relationships.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne documents Ring Blessing as a ceremony where students honor the Duquesne ring and commit to carry the university’s spirit forward with integrity, leadership and compassion.
cards.access_notes: Participation conditions, ring requirements, ceremony date and venue are not stated on the traditions page; verify them with the organizer.

cards.title: Let Faculty Serve Breakfast Before Exams
cards.subtitle: Pancakes, games and study-break activities arrive late at night
cards.notes: Pause exam preparation for breakfast and stress-relief activities once Duquesne posts the current date, venue and entry details.
cards.short_summary: Before exams, the usual faculty-student roles flip across the breakfast counter.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne says Late-Night Breakfast occurs just before exams, with faculty and staff serving students breakfast alongside games, music, giveaways and stress-relief activities.
cards.access_notes: The university confirms that breakfast is served late at night but does not publish a current clock time, venue, eligibility or cost on this page.

warnings: The official traditions page provides no publication date, so source_published_at is null for every card.
Event dates, prices and most venue details are absent from the source; access_notes preserve those limitations rather than inferring them.
